Uhhh sorry stupid mistake, that should've been optional but I missed something silly. Update now and it should work.

The reason for this update is that in torch 2.7.0 nightly there this feature:

```
Full FP16 Accmumulation in FP16 GEMMs
-------------------------------------

Certain GPUs have increased performance when doing _all_ FP16 GEMM accumulation
in FP16, at the cost of numerical precision and greater likelihood of overflow.
Note that this setting only has an effect on GPUs of compute capability 7.0 (Volta)
or newer.

This behavior can be enabled via:

  torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_fp16_accumulation = True
```

Which makes using fp16 as the base_precision run the model lot faster, even if you use fp8 quantization.
I can confirm this is fixed - Thank you!

There's no block swapping enabled as I'm just using the tiny 1.3B model. Occupancy while inferencing is ~65%, post-completion it stays at 55% and on the next run it goes to 95% + shared memory. 10GB vram and 768x768x81.

I was watching it complete live just now, and noticed that the vram did drop to ~11% after the sampler finished, but then pushed up to 95% when doing the vae decoding. It reduced to 52% after decoding was completed, but no further. Some sort of decoding cache not being emptied?

I think I found it, there's some caching in the VAE that's not cleared, I could replicate this with simply loading VAE and encoding something, it would use ~2GB VRAM no matter what I did. There was a function already in the VAE to clear it, so just calling it frees it all. 

Thanks for raising the issue, this was a lot of wasted VRAM even for normal inference.
Awesome, thanks!
